summary: In this story, on a school trip to Egypt, a curious student works with a real archaeologist to decode hieroglyphic inscriptions and learns historical facts about how the pyramids were built and what ancient Egyptians believed.
introduce: Act out a short mime, such as checking your watch and tapping your foot, and ask students how you feel and how they know. Explain that in “The Puzzle of the Pyramid” they will use clues in the same way to work out what the writer does not say directly.

keyTerms.def: a picture-sign used by ancient Egyptians to write words
a scientist who studies old objects and places to learn about the past
a picture or shape cut into a hard material like stone or wood

challengeTerms.def: an object made by people in the past that tells us about their lives
a life some people believe continues after a person dies
to figure out the meaning of a message written in signs or symbols

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that ancient Egyptian beliefs about gods are too strange for modern students to learn about? Use evidence from the story to explain.
struggling: Read the first part of the story aloud together, review hieroglyph, archaeologist, and carving, and let weak readers answer “What clue tells you that?” questions using sentence starters.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use artifact, afterlife, and decode in a short paragraph that makes an inference that the story does not state and support it with two clues.
